title: The highest celestial degree requires the covenant of marriage
setting: In mid-May 1843 Joseph Smith visited Ramus, also called Macedonia, Illinois. On 16 May he taught William Clayton and Benjamin and Melissa Johnson at the Johnson home. His subject was priesthood and the sealing of marriage. On 17 May he preached on 2 Peter 1 and spoke again that evening. Clayton recorded these teachings in his journal, and they were later combined as section 131.
summary: The section opens with three heavens or degrees within the celestial glory. To obtain the highest, a man must enter an order of the priesthood. A bracketed note explains this as the new and everlasting covenant of marriage. Without it, he may enter another degree but cannot have an increase. A note dated 17 May defines the “more sure word of prophecy”. It means knowing by revelation that one is sealed up to eternal life. The section says no one can be saved in ignorance. It ends by saying all spirit is matter, too fine to be seen now.

contextNote.title: Marriage as an order of the priesthood
contextNote.text: Verse 1 divides the celestial glory into three degrees. Verse 2 then states what reaches the highest one. Its answer is “this order of the priesthood,” which the bracketed note calls the covenant of marriage. Verses 3–4 state the result of not entering it: “that is the end of his kingdom”. The missing blessing is named as “increase”. Verse 5 adds the idea of knowing that one is “sealed up unto eternal life”. In this passage, the order is a sealed marriage covenant tied to eternal increase.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 129–132 teaches that Heavenly Father made it possible for families to be eternal. How do verses 2–4 connect marriage with what this section calls “increase”?

jsp.title: Instruction, 16 May 1843, as Reported by William Clayton

reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives Ramus, Illinois, 16 and 17 May 1843, with verse 5 dated 17 May. The JSP page loaded showed only the source note, so I read the historical introduction through the JSP Doctrine and Covenants Study Companion (churchofjesuschrist.org jsp-revelations dc-131), which joins the 16 May instruction and two 17 May discourses. It places the teaching at the Benjamin F. Johnson home with William Clayton and the Johnsons present. I believe the bracketed phrase in verse 2 is a later editorial insertion, but did not confirm when it was added. William Clayton is not in people-ids and is not named in the text.
